Common_Names_Hindi: Tezaabiyath; Gale me jalana; Acid Reflux
Primary_Symptoms: Heartburn; Acid regurgitation; Epigastric burning
Secondary_Symptoms: Dysphagia; Chronic dry cough; Globus sensation; Waterbrash
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khane ke baad gale me tezaab aata hai?; 2. Chero me ya chhati me jalan hoti hai?; 3. Raat ko letne par takleef badhti hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Sodium Alginate + Potassium Bicarbonate syrup 10 mL after meals; Magaldrate + Simethicone syrup
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Long-term PPI use needs doctor review (osteoporosis, B12 deficiency risk); Caution in severe renal or hepatic impairment
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate head end of bed by 6 inches; Do not lie down within 3 hours of meals; Avoid spicy, oily, citrus, caffeine, and late-night heavy food
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy; 24-hour Ambulatory pH-impedance Monitoring
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Persistent dysphagia or odynophagia; Unexplained weight loss; Hematemesis; Melena

Common_Names_Hindi: Pet me gas; Acidity; Hazma kharab
Primary_Symptoms: Epigastric burning pain; Bloating; Belching; Nausea
Secondary_Symptoms: Sour eructations; Early satiety; Epigastric fullness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet ke upar hisse me meetha dard ya jalan hai?; 2. Khana der se hazam hota hai?; 3. Khate hi pet phool jata hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Magaldrate + Simethicone oral suspension 10 mL TDS SOS; Oral Rehydration Salts
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Domperidone caution in cardiac arrhythmias or prolonged QT interval; Avoid NSAIDs as they worsen hyperacidity
Home_Care_Advice: Drink plenty of warm water; Sip chamomile or fennel tea; Small frequent meals; Avoid carbonated drinks, alcohol, and smoking
Lab_Investigations: None routinely required for acute episodes; Routine Blood Sugar; Upper GI Endoscopy if non-responsive
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe unremitting abdominal pain; Repeated vomiting; Black tarry stools; Chest pain radiating to arm

Primary_Symptoms: Epigastric pain (burning/gnawing); Pain related to meals (postprandial/hunger pain); Nausea
Secondary_Symptoms: Bloating; Belching; Vomiting; Anorexia; Weight loss
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khane ke baad dard badhta hai ya kam hota hai?; 2. Raat me dard se neend khulti hai?; 3. Dard peth ki taraf jata hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Sukralfate 1g suspension 10 mL QID (before meals & bedtime); Antacids
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid ALL NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Aspirin) as they worsen ulcers; Use Paracetamol for pain; Long-term PPI needs doctor review
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid spicy, acidic, fried foods; Complete cessation of smoking and alcohol; Bland diet; Avoid late-night eating
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy with biopsy; Stool Antigen Test for H. pylori; CBC (check for anemia)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hematemesis (vomiting blood or coffee-ground material); Melena (black tarry stools); Sudden severe board-like abdominal rigidity (perforation)

Common_Names_Hindi: H. pylori Infection; Pet ka bacteriya
Primary_Symptoms: Chronic epigastric burning; Persistent dyspepsia; Postprandial fullness; Nausea
Secondary_Symptoms: Bloating; Frequent belching; Halitosis; Loss of appetite
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Acidity ki dawai lene par bhi dard bar-bar hota hai?; 2. Pet me lagatar jalan rehti hai?; 3. Stool antigen test positive aaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clarithromycin + Amoxicillin + Rabeprazole (Standard Indian Triple Therapy)
Supportive_Medicines: Probiotics (Saccharomyces boulardii 250 mg BD); Sukralfate suspension 10 mL QID
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 1000 mg Clarithromycin / 2000 mg Amoxicillin / 40 mg Rabeprazole
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Strictly complete full 14-day regimen to prevent antibiotic resistance; Hypersensitivity to Penicillins or Macrolides; Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Take all medications strictly as directed; Bland non-spicy diet; Avoid alcohol during treatment; Good hand hygiene
Lab_Investigations: H. pylori Stool Antigen Test; Urea Breath Test; Endoscopic Biopsy RDT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Massive GI bleeding (hematemesis/melena); Severe persistent vomiting; Unintentional rapid weight loss

Common_Names_Hindi: IBS-D; Pet ki marod aur dast; Chinta se dast
Primary_Symptoms: Abdominal pain relieved by defecation; Frequent loose stools; Stool urgency
Secondary_Symptoms: Mucus in stool; Bloating; Feeling of incomplete evacuation; Stress-related exacerbation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khate hi latrine bhagna padta hai?; 2. Subah-subah 3-4 baar dast hota hai?; 3. Latrine jaane par pet dard me aaram milta hai?
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (8 hourly for Rifaximin) / BD SOS (Dicyclomine)
Supportive_Medicines: Probiotics (VSL#3 / Enterogermina); Loperamide 2 mg SOS (short-term strictly); Psyllium husk
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid Loperamide if high fever or blood in stool present; Dicyclomine caution in glaucoma and BPH
Home_Care_Advice: Follow Low-FODMAP diet; Avoid dairy, artificial sweeteners, caffeine, and spicy food; Stress management (yoga/meditation)
Lab_Investigations: Stool Routine & Microscopy (rule out infection); Complete Blood Count; Anti-tTG IgA (rule out Celiac disease)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Blood in stool; Unexplained weight loss; Nocturnal diarrhea awakening from sleep; Onset after age 50

Common_Names_Hindi: IBS-C; Pet ki marod aur kabz
Primary_Symptoms: Abdominal pain relieved by defecation; Infrequent hard lumpy stools; Straining
Secondary_Symptoms: Bloating; Abdominal distension; Sensation of incomplete evacuation; Flatulence
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kabz ke sath peth me marod aur dard hota hai?; 2. Latrine hone ke baad dard kam hota hai?; 3. Stool hard aur chhota aata hai?
Dosage_Frequency: BD or TDS (Mebeverine 20 min before meals)
Supportive_Medicines: Polyethylene Glycol (PEG 3350) 17 g OD SOS; Probiotics; Linaclotide under specialist guidance
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Ensure high fluid intake with bulk-forming laxatives to prevent bowel impaction; Mebeverine caution in severe hepatic impairment
Home_Care_Advice: Gradually increase dietary fiber (fruits, vegetables, oats); Drink at least 3 liters of water daily; Regular daily physical activity
Lab_Investigations: CBC; Thyroid Function Test (TSH); Stool Routine; Colonoscopy if red flags present
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rectal bleeding; Sudden severe change in bowel habits; Unintentional weight loss; Severe abdominal distension

Common_Names_Hindi: Khana na hazam hona; Pet ka phoolna
Primary_Symptoms: Postprandial fullness; Early satiety; Epigastric pain or burning
Secondary_Symptoms: Upper abdominal bloating; Nausea; Belching; Anorexia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khate hi pet bhari ho jata hai?; 2. Thoda sa khate hi lagta hai pet bhar gaya?; 3. Epigastric region me jalan rehti hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Digestive enzyme syrup (Diastase + Pepsin) 10 mL after meals; Simethicone 80 mg TDS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Levosulpiride can cause hyperprolactinemia, extrapyramidal symptoms, and drowsiness; Caution in GI hemorrhage or mechanical obstruction
Home_Care_Advice: Eat small, frequent meals; Chew food thoroughly and slowly; Avoid fatty, spicy, and deep-fried foods; Walk for 15 min post meals
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy (to rule out structural disease); H. pylori testing; Routine biochemistry
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progressive dysphagia; Frequent vomiting; Persistent anorexia; GI bleeding; Anemia

Primary_Symptoms: Infrequent bowel movements (<3/week); Hard dry stools; Excessive straining
Secondary_Symptoms: Abdominal discomfort; Mild bloating; Sensation of incomplete evacuation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kitne din se latrine nahi hui hai?; 2. Stool pass karne me zord lagana padta hai?; 3. Pet me tez dard to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Bisacodyl OR Liquid Paraffin + Milk of Magnesia
Supportive_Medicines: Psyllium husk 1-2 spoons with warm water; Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Do not use stimulant laxatives (Bisacodyl) continuously for >7 days to prevent laxative dependence and cathartic colon; Contraindicated in intestinal obstruction or acute surgical abdomen
Home_Care_Advice: Drink warm water early morning; Eat fiber-rich foods (prunes, papaya, oats); Avoid low-fiber processed foods; Do not ignore urge to defecate
Lab_Investigations: None routinely required for acute mild constipation
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Complete inability to pass gas or stool with severe vomiting (intestinal obstruction); Severe sharp abdominal pain; Blood in stool

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent infrequent defecation (<3/week for >3 months); Difficulty evacuation; Straining
Secondary_Symptoms: Lumpy/hard stools; Abdominal distension; Anorectal distress; Dependence on laxatives
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kabz mahino se hai?; 2. Bina laxative ke latrine nahi hoti?; 3. Piles ya fissure ki dikkat bani hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Psyllium husk 7 g daily; Prucalopride 1-2 mg OD (under specialist supervision)
Precautions_Contraindications: Caution in diabetic patients with Lactulose (monitor blood sugar); Ensure high fluid intake with osmotic laxatives; Avoid in galactosemia
Home_Care_Advice: High fiber diet (25-30g daily); Drink 3-4 liters of water daily; Regular daily walking/exercise; Establish fixed toilet routine after meals
Lab_Investigations: Thyroid Function Test (TSH); Serum Calcium; Fasting Blood Sugar; Colonoscopy if onset after 50 years
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Blood in stool; Unexplained weight loss; Severe abdominal cramps; Fecal impaction signs; Family history of colorectal cancer

Primary_Symptoms: Painless bright red bleeding per rectum (drip/jet); Anal mass prolapsing on defecation
Secondary_Symptoms: Anal pruritus; Perianal discomfort; Mucus discharge; Mild soreness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Stool ke sath ya baad me fresh lal khoon tapakta hai?; 2. Mosa (mass) bahar aata hai latrine ke waqt?; 3. Dard hota hai ya painless hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Calcium Dobesilate OR Micronized Purified Flavonoid Fraction (MPFF - Diosmin + Hesperidin)
Dosage_Frequency: BD (12 hourly for Dobesilate) / BD or TDS (Daflon)
Supportive_Medicines: Lignocaine + Hydrocortisone / Anovate ointment topically; Warm Sitz bath; Liquid Paraffin syrup 10 mL at bedtime
Precautions_Contraindications: Do not use steroid-containing topical ointments for >14 days continuously to prevent perianal skin atrophy; Avoid straining at stool
Home_Care_Advice: Warm Sitz bath 2-3 times daily for 15 mins; High fiber diet; Drink plenty of fluids; Avoid sitting on toilet for extended periods
Lab_Investigations: Digital Rectal Examination (DRE); Proctoscopy; Anoscopy; Sigmoidoscopy if age >45
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Profuse unremitting rectal bleeding causing dizziness/pallor; Severe acute perianal pain (thrombosed hemorrhoid); Incarcerated/strangulated prolapsed mass

Common_Names_Hindi: Fissure; Latrine ki jagah katha hona; Katna
Primary_Symptoms: Severe sharp knife-like pain during and after defecation; Streak of bright red blood on stool/tissue
Secondary_Symptoms: Perianal sphincter spasm; Fear of defecation; Constipation; Anal itching
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Latrine karne ke waqt aur baad me tez kaatne waala dard hota hai?; 2. Stool par lal patti jaisa khoon aata hai?; 3. Dard ghan-to tak rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Diltiazem 2% gel OR Glyceryl Trinitrate (GTN) 0.2% ointment (topical application)
Supportive_Medicines: Warm Sitz bath TDS; Liquid Paraffin + Milk of Magnesia 15 mL at bedtime; Paracetamol 650 mg SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; GTN ointment can cause transient severe headache and hypotension; Avoid systemic NSAIDs if GI bleeding risk exists
Home_Care_Advice: Warm Sitz bath for 15 mins after every bowel movement; Keep stool soft with osmotic laxatives; Avoid straining; Eat high fiber diet
Lab_Investigations: Proctoscopy / Visual inspection of anal verge (gentle evaluation)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Unbearable unremitting perianal pain; Fever with perianal swelling/induration (perianal abscess); Non-healing fissure >6 weeks

Primary_Symptoms: Usually asymptomatic; Mild dull ache in right upper abdomen; Mild fatigue
Secondary_Symptoms: Hepatomegaly; Mild elevation of AST/ALT; Fullness in right hypochondrium
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ultrasound me fatty liver grade 1 aaya hai?; 2. Weight ya pet ki charbi zyada hai?; 3. Blood sugar ya cholesterol bada hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Saroglitazar OR Vitamin E (400 IU) / Ursodeoxycholic Acid (UDCA)
Supportive_Medicines: Multivitamins with B-complex; Lifestyle modifications (diet & exercise primary)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions; NSAIDs and alcohol MUST be strictly avoided; Caution with Vitamin E in high dose long-term
Home_Care_Advice: Strict dietary calorie restriction (low fat, low refined carbs/sugar); 150 min/week moderate aerobic exercise; Aim for 7-10% weight loss; Zero alcohol intake
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test (SGOT, SGPT, Bilirubin); Ultrasound Abdomen; Lipid Profile; Fasting Blood Sugar; FibroScan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Onset of jaundice; Abdominal distension (ascites); Easy bruising or bleeding; Sudden right upper quadrant severe pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Sharab se jigar ki bimari; Alcoholic Hepatitis
Primary_Symptoms: Anorexia; Right upper quadrant discomfort; Jaundice; Hepatomegaly
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Low fever; Nausea; Muscle wasting; Spider nevi; Palmar erythema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kitne saal se aur kitni sharab peete hain?; 2. Aankhein peeli hui hain ya pet bada hai?; 3. Bhookh kam lagti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Silibinin / Silymarin OR Metadoxine / Ursodeoxycholic Acid
Supportive_Medicines: B-complex vitamins (Thiamine 100 mg daily); Choline; Corticosteroids (Prednisolone) if severe alcoholic hepatitis
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions; NSAIDs and alcohol MUST be strictly avoided; Absolute alcohol abstinence mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: STRICT TOTAL ABSTINENCE FROM ALCOHOL IS MANDATORY; High calorie, high protein diet (unless encephalopathic); Hydration; Nutritional support
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test (AST/ALT ratio >2, High Bilirubin); CBC; Prothrombin Time/INR; USG Abdomen; FibroScan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Deepening jaundice; Hematemesis or melena; Confusion/drowsiness (encephalopathy); High fever with abdominal pain (SBP); Anuria

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe epigastric pain radiating to back; Persistent vomiting; Abdominal tenderness
Secondary_Symptoms: Fever; Tachycardia; Abdominal distension; Paralytic ileus; Hypotension
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet ke piche kamar tak tez dard phaila hai?; 2. Ulti ruk nahi rahi hai?; 3. Sharab ya gallstone ki history hai?
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Pantoprazole; Injection Tramadol; IV Fluids (Ringer Lactate)
Supportive_Medicines: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation; IV Analgesics (Buprenorphine/Tramadol); Parenteral nutrition if oral intake delayed
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home painkillers, laxatives, or antacids; Strict Nil By Mouth (NPO)
Home_Care_Advice: Keep patient Nil By Mouth (NPO); Immediate emergency transfer to hospital with ICU and surgical facilities; Do not give oral water or food while reaching hospital
Lab_Investigations: Serum Lipase (>3x upper limit); Serum Amylase; Contrast-Enhanced CT (CECT) Abdomen; USG Abdomen; CBC; RFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Severe hypotension/shock; Anuria; Acute breathlessness (ARDS); Altered mental status

Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent severe epigastric pain radiating to back; Steatorrhea (foul pale oily stool); Weight loss
Secondary_Symptoms: Diabetes mellitus (secondary); Bloating; Malabsorption; Nausea
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet me dard hamesha rehta hai aur peth tak jata hai?; 2. Latrine me tel/ghee jaisa chikna aata hai?; 3. Weight bahut kam ho gaya hai?
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (with every major meal and snack)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K); Insulin if diabetic
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Take enzyme capsules WITH meals, do not crush or chew granules; Strict smoking and alcohol cessation
Home_Care_Advice: Eat small frequent low-fat meals; Complete abstinence from alcohol and smoking; Take pancreatic enzymes with every meal; Vitamin supplementation
Lab_Investigations: Fecal Elastase-1 test; CT Abdomen / MRCP; Fasting Blood Sugar / HbA1c; Serum Lipase
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden severe acute flare up of pain; Intractable vomiting; Uncontrolled blood sugar spikes; Jaundice (biliary obstruction)

Common_Names_Hindi: Pitte ki pathri ka dard; Gallstone Colic
Primary_Symptoms: Epigastric or Right Upper Quadrant pain radiating to right shoulder/scapula; Postprandial pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Diaphoresis; Dyspepsia; Bloating
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana (khas kar oily) khane ke 1-2 ghante baad daahine taraf tez dard hota hai?; 2. Dard kandhe tak jata hai?; 3. Dard kuch ghanto me shuru aur khatam hota hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Ursodeoxycholic acid 300 mg BD (limited role for cholesterol stones); Antacid
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; NSAIDs caution in peptic ulcer; Definitive treatment for symptomatic gallstones is Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid fatty, greasy, fried, and heavy meals; Maintain ideal body weight with gradual weight loss; Sip warm fluids
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Abdomen (Gold standard); Liver Function Test; CBC
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Pain persisting >6 hours (Acute Cholecystitis); High fever with chills/rigors; Jaundice (peeli aankhein - choledocholithiasis)

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent Right Upper Quadrant pain (>6 hours); RUQ tenderness with Murphy's sign; Fever
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Anorexia; Tachycardia; Guarding
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Daahine taraf pet ke upar hisse me lagatar tez dard hai?; 2. Chhune par tez dard aur saans rukti hai (Murphy sign)?; 3. Bukhar hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Cefoperazone + Sulbactam (IV initial) then Cefixime OR Ciprofloxacin
Supportive_Medicines: Hyoscine butylbromide 10 mg TDS SOS; IV fluids; Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy evaluation
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy recommended; Caution in cephalosporin allergy
Home_Care_Advice: Hospital admission usually required; Low fat liquid diet initially; Complete rest; Do not apply local heat to abdomen
Lab_Investigations: USG Abdomen (thickened gallbladder wall >4mm, pericholecystic fluid); CBC (leukocytosis); LFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High grade fever with rigors; Deep jaundice; Peritoneal rigidity (perforation); Septic shock signs

Common_Names_Hindi: Aant ka zakhm; Ulcerative Colitis; UC
Primary_Symptoms: Bloody diarrhea with mucus; Abdominal cramps/tenesmus; Rectal urgency
Secondary_Symptoms: Fever; Fatigue; Anemia; Weight loss; Arthralgia; Small frequent bowel movements
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dast me khoon aur aao (mucus) mahino se aa raha hai?; 2. Din me 6-10 baar latrine jana padta hai?; 3. Latrine ke baad bhi lagta hai pet saaf nahi hua?
Supportive_Medicines: Prednisolone oral (for acute flares under specialist); Mesalamine enema/suppository; Folic Acid 5 mg
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Nephrotoxicity risk with Mesalamine (monitor renal function); Avoid NSAIDs as they trigger UC flares; Use Paracetamol for pain
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain low-residue diet during flares; Avoid dairy, spicy foods, alcohol, and caffeine; Ensure high hydration; Take medications strictly uninterrupted
Lab_Investigations: Colonoscopy with biopsy (Gold standard); Fecal Calprotectin; CBC; ESR/CRP; Stool routine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe profuse bloody diarrhea (>10 times/day); High fever with toxic megacolon signs; Severe abdominal distension and rebound tenderness; Severe anemia/hypotension

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic right lower quadrant abdominal pain; Non-bloody or bloody diarrhea; Weight loss
Secondary_Symptoms: Fever; Malabsorption; Perianal fissures/fistulae; Fatigue; Oral aphthous ulcers
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet ke daahine aur niche hisse me dard rehta hai?; 2. Dast aur weight loss mahino se hai?; 3. Anus ke paas koi zakhm ya nali (fistula) bani hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Budencof (Budesonide capsules 3 mg TDS); Iron supplements; Vitamin B12; Nutritional supplements
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Azathioprine causes bone marrow suppression and hepatotoxicity; Avoid NSAIDs as they trigger flares; Use Paracetamol for pain
Home_Care_Advice: Eat small nutrient-dense low-fiber meals during flares; High protein diet; Avoid smoking completely (smoking worsens Crohn's); Hydrate well
Lab_Investigations: Ileocolonoscopy with biopsy; CT/MR Enterography; CBC; ESR/CRP; Serum Vitamin B12 and Ferritin
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Complete intestinal obstruction (severe vomiting, no gas/stool); High fever with abdominal mass/abscess; Peranal massive bleeding; Fistula discharge flare

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic diarrhea; Abdominal distension/bloating; Weight loss; Malabsorption
Secondary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Anemia; Recurrent aphthous ulcers; Dermatitis herpetiformis; Stunted growth
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Wheat (gehu/roti) khane ke baad pet kharab hota hai?; 2. Dast aur weight loss mahino se hai?; 3. Blood test me blood count kam rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Strict Gluten-Free Diet (GFD) - No primary drug
Supportive_Medicines: Iron, Calcium, Vitamin D3, Vitamin B12, and Folic Acid supplements
Precautions_Contraindications: Do not start Gluten-Free Diet BEFORE diagnostic testing (causes false negative antibody and biopsy results); Check all food labels for hidden gluten
Home_Care_Advice: STRICT LIFELONG GLUTEN-FREE DIET (strictly exclude wheat, barley, rye); Use separate cooking utensils; Eat rice, corn, pulses, millet ( बाजरा/ज्वार)
Lab_Investigations: Anti-tissue Transglutaminase (anti-tTG IgA) antibodies; Total Serum IgA; Duodenal Endoscopic Biopsy (Marsh grading)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe malnutrition or dehydration (celiac crisis); Severe refractory diarrhea; Peripheral edema (hypoalbuminemia)

Primary_Symptoms: Abdominal cramps, flatulence, bloating, and watery diarrhea 30 min to 2 hours post dairy intake
Secondary_Symptoms: Borborygmi (stomach rumbling); Nausea; Explosive loose stools
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Doodh, dahi ya paneer khane ke 1-2 ghante baad pet me marod aur dast hota hai?; 2. Pet me gurgurahat aur gas hoti hai?; 3. Bina milk products ke pet normal rehta hai?
Dosage_Frequency: Taken WITH first bite of dairy food
Supportive_Medicines: Probiotics; Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 supplements
Precautions_Contraindications: Ensure adequate dietary Calcium and Vitamin D intake when excluding dairy; Differentiate from true milk protein allergy
Home_Care_Advice: Limit or avoid liquid cows milk; Switch to lactose-free milk, curd, or plant milk (soy/almond); Consume curd/yoghurt (better tolerated)
Lab_Investigations: Hydrogen Breath Test; Stool pH and Reducing Substances Test; Clinical elimination test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe persistent diarrhea causing dehydration; Significant unintentional weight loss; Blood in stool

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent abdominal bloating/distension immediately post meals; Excessive flatulence; Diarrhea or constipation
Secondary_Symptoms: Abdominal pain; Weight loss; Malabsorption (B12 deficiency); Fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khate hi pet fula-fula lagta hai?; 2. Gas aur dast ki dikkat rehti hai?; 3. Probiotics lene par symptoms badhte hain?
Supportive_Medicines: Prokinetic agents (Itopride 50 mg BD post-antibiotic); Digestive enzymes; Vitamin B12
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid routine use of systemic broad-spectrum antibiotics; Avoid excessive use of PPIs as reduced stomach acid promotes SIBO
Home_Care_Advice: Eat low-FODMAP diet short-term; Allow 4-5 hours gap between meals (supports Migrating Motor Complex); Avoid refined sugars
Lab_Investigations: Glucose or Lactulose Hydrogen/Methane Breath Test (Gold standard); Endoscopic jejunal aspirate culture
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe unremitting abdominal pain; Rapid unintentional weight loss; Severe anemia; Profuse watery diarrhea

Primary_Symptoms: Foul-smelling watery/greasy diarrhea; Abdominal cramps; Bloating; Profuse sulfurous belching
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Fatigue; Weight loss; Anorexia; Excessive flatulence
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dast se saday hua andey (sulfur) jaisi badboo aati hai?; 2. Pet me gurgurahat aur marod hai?; 3. Dushit paani ya bahar ka khana khaya tha?
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS); Probiotics (Saccharomyces boulardii)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; STRICT AVOIDANCE OF ALCOHOL during and for 72h post-treatment (disulfiram-like reaction); Caution in liver disease
Home_Care_Advice: Drink only boiled or filtered water; Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly; Practice strict hand hygiene; ORS hydration
Lab_Investigations: Stool Routine & Microscopy (Giardia lamblia trophozoites/cysts x 3 samples); Stool Giardia Antigen ELISA
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, dry mouth, oliguria); High fever; Blood in stool; Symptoms persisting post-treatment

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset loose watery stools (>3/day) during or post travel; Abdominal cramps
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Low fever; Bloating; Urgency
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Safar ke dauran ya turant baad dast shuru hua hai?; 2. Din me kitni baar latrine jana pad raha hai?; 3. Bukhar ya ulti hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS); Zinc 20 mg OD; Racecadotril 100 mg TDS SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Fluoroquinolone caution (tendonitis risk); Avoid Loperamide if high fever or dysentery (bloody stool) present
Home_Care_Advice: Aggressive oral hydration with ORS, coconut water; Drink bottled/boiled water only; Avoid street food, raw salads, and ice cubes
Lab_Investigations: Stool Routine & Microscopy if non-responsive; Serum Electrolytes if dehydrated
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever (>102F); Bloody stools (dysentery); Inability to retain oral fluids; Severe dehydration; Symptoms >5 days

Primary_Symptoms: Periumbilical pain migrating to Right Lower Quadrant (McBurney point); Anorexia (Hamburger sign)
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Low fever; Abdominal guarding & rebound tenderness; Pain on walking
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard pehle naabhi ke paas shuru hokar daahine taraf niche gaya hai?; 2. Khana khane ka bilkul man nahi hai?; 3. Khaansne ya chalne par daahine taraf tez dard hota hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Emergency Laparoscopic or Open Appendectomy; IV Antibiotics; IV Fluids
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home painkillers, laxatives, or hot water bags (risk of appendix rupture/peritonitis); Strict NPO
Home_Care_Advice: Keep patient strictly Nil By Mouth (NPO); Immediate transfer to surgical hospital; Do NOT massage abdomen or give laxatives while reaching hospital
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Abdomen & Pelvis; Contrast CT Abdomen; CBC (High TLC with neutrophilia); CRP
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; High fever with sudden generalized severe abdominal rigidity (perforated appendix); Septic shock

Primary_Symptoms: Periumbilical abdominal pain; Anorexia or excessive hunger; Weight loss; Anemia (Hookworm)
Secondary_Symptoms: Pruritus ani; Passage of worms in stool; Vomiting; Pica (eating dirt); Cough (Loffler syndrome)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Latrine me keede nikalte hain?; 2. Pet me naabhi ke paas dard rehta hai?; 3. Raat ko anus me khujli ya mitti khane ka man karta hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Iron + Folic acid syrup/tablets (for hookworm anemia); Syrup Piperazine
Precautions_Contraindications: Avoid in first trimester of pregnancy; Caution in hepatic impairment; Chew Albendazole tablet thoroughly before swallowing for optimal effect
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict hand hygiene; Cut fingernails short; Wash fruits/vegetables thoroughly; Do not walk barefoot on soil (prevents hookworm); Treat all family members
Lab_Investigations: Stool Routine & Microscopy (Ova/Cysts identification); CBC (Eosinophilia, low Hemoglobin)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe acute abdominal pain with intestinal obstruction (roundworm bolus); Repeated vomiting of worms; Severe pallor/anemia

Primary_Symptoms: Intense perianal pruritus, strictly worst at night; Irritability; Restless sleep
Secondary_Symptoms: Perianal erythema/excoriation; Passage of small white thread-like worms at night
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Raat ko sote samay anus ke paas tez khujli hoti hai?; 2. Raat ko chhote safed dhage jaise keede dikhte hain?; 3. Neend baar-baar toot-ti hai?
Dosage_Frequency: Single dose (Must repeat second dose after exactly 14 days)
Duration_Days: Single dose on Day 1, repeat single dose on Day 14
Supportive_Medicines: Calamine lotion perianally; Iron supplements if needed
Precautions_Contraindications: TREAT ENTIRE HOUSEHOLD SIMULTANEOUSLY to prevent reinfection; Contraindicated in first trimester of pregnancy
Home_Care_Advice: Wash all bedsheets, pajamas, and underwear in hot water on Day 1; Cut nails short; Daily morning bath; Prevent scratching perianal area
Lab_Investigations: Graham Scotch Tape test (applied to perianal area early morning before bath)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Secondary bacterial skin infection from severe scratching; Vulvovaginitis in young girls; Persistent symptoms despite 2 treatment cycles

Common_Names_Hindi: Pet ka dhere chalna; Delayed Gastric Emptying
Primary_Symptoms: Nausea; Repeated vomiting of undigested food hours post meals; Early satiety; Epigastric fullness
Secondary_Symptoms: Postprandial bloating; Epigastric pain; Weight loss; Uncontrolled blood sugar fluctuations
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khane ke kai ghante baad bhi undigested khane ki ulti hoti hai?; 2. Thoda sa khate hi pet bhar jata hai?; 3. Aapko Purani Diabetes hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Erythromycin 250 mg TDS (low dose prokinetic under specialist guidance); Insulin adjustment
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Metoclopramide carries Black Box warning for tardive dyskinesia (do not use >12 weeks); Domperidone QT prolongation risk
Home_Care_Advice: Eat 5-6 small liquid/blenderized low-fat low-fiber meals daily; Walk after meals; Avoid lying down for 2 hours post meals; Strict glycemic control
Lab_Investigations: Gastric Emptying Study (Scintigraphy - Gold standard); Upper GI Endoscopy (rule out obstruction); HbA1c
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Persistent intractable vomiting causing dehydration; Severe ketoacidosis/hypoglycemia spikes; Severe weight loss

Common_Names_Hindi: Grasanali me sujan; Food pipe infection/inflammation
Primary_Symptoms: Severe odynophagia (pain on swallowing); Dysphagia; Retrosternal chest pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Heartburn; Acid regurgitation; Epigastric burning; Hematemesis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana nigalne me chhati me tez dard hota hai?; 2. Chhati ke beech me meetha/tez dard rehta hai?; 3. Acidity ki dikkat purani hai ya koi tablet bina paani ke li thi?
Supportive_Medicines: Sukralfate 1g suspension 10 mL QID (1 hour before meals); Local anesthetic antacid gel (Mucaine Gel)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Swallow all pills with plenty of water in an upright position (prevents pill-induced esophagitis); Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Eat soft, bland, room-temperature foods; Avoid spicy, hot, acidic, citrus, and hard crunchy foods; Drink water with pills; Do not lie down immediately post meals
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy with mucosal biopsy (Gold standard); Cytology for Candida/HSV/CMV if immunocompromised
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Complete inability to swallow liquids/saliva; Severe retrosternal pain radiating to back; Hematemesis (vomiting blood); Unexplained weight loss

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden hematemesis (bright red blood in vomit) following severe retching or forceful vomiting
Secondary_Symptoms: Epigastric or retrosternal pain; Melena; Dizziness; Tachycardia; Pallor
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bahut tez ulti/uchhal aane ke baad vomit me fresh khoon aaya hai?; 2. Sharab peene ke baad aisa hua hai?; 3. Chakkar aa rahe hain?
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Pantoprazole 80 mg IV bolus; IV Fluids
Supportive_Medicines: IV Pantoprazole infusion; Endoscopic Hemoclip / Banding / Epinephrine injection; Blood transfusion if needed
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home painkillers, NSAIDs, antacids, or food/water; Strict Nil By Mouth (NPO)
Home_Care_Advice: Keep patient strictly Nil By Mouth (NPO); Absolute bed rest; Immediate emergency transfer to hospital with endoscopy facilities
Lab_Investigations: Emergent Upper GI Endoscopy; Complete Blood Count (Hb/Hct); Prothrombin Time/INR; Cross-matching blood
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Profuse continuous hematemesis; Syncope/Hypotension; Severe pallor

Common_Names_Hindi: Aant me gubbare ki sujan; Diverticulitis
Primary_Symptoms: Persistent Left Lower Quadrant abdominal pain; Fever; Sudden change in bowel habits (constipation/diarrhea)
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Vomiting; Abdominal distension/tenderness; Dysuria (if bladder adjacent)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet ke baaye (left) aur niche hisse me lagatar dard hai?; 2. Bukhar ke sath kabz ya dast hai?; 3. Chhune par baaye taraf tez dard hota hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Paracetamol 650 mg SOS for fever/pain; Clear liquid diet initially
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid NSAIDs and opioids as they increase risk of diverticular perforation; Ciprofloxacin tendonitis risk
Home_Care_Advice: Clear liquid diet for 2-3 days during acute phase, then advance to low-fiber soft diet, then high-fiber long term post recovery; Adequate fluid intake
Lab_Investigations: Contrast-Enhanced CT Abdomen & Pelvis (Gold standard); CBC (Leukocytosis); CRP; Colonoscopy CONTRAINDICATED in acute phase
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever with chills; Generalized severe abdominal rigidity & rebound tenderness (perforation/peritonitis); Inability to tolerate oral liquids; Severe rectal bleeding

Primary_Symptoms: Rectal bleeding; Tenesmus (constant painful urge to defecate); Rectal pain/fullness
Secondary_Symptoms: Mucopurulent rectal discharge; Diarrhea; Lower left abdominal pain; Pruritus ani
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Latrine ke muuh (rectum) me dard aur bharapan rehta hai?; 2. Khoon aur pus/mucus nikalta hai?; 3. Baar-baar latrine jaane ki jhuti urge hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mesalamine suppositories/enema OR Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole (if infectious)
Dosage_Frequency: BD or OD at bedtime (Suppository) / BD (Ciprofloxacin)
Supportive_Medicines: Warm Sitz bath TDS; Hydrocortisone acetate enema; Paracetamol 500 mg SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid NSAIDs as they worsen mucosal inflammation; Ensure proper insertion technique for suppositories
Home_Care_Advice: Warm Sitz bath 2-3 times daily; Maintain soft stools with osmotic laxatives (PEG); Avoid spicy/irritant foods; Proper perianal hygiene
Lab_Investigations: Proctosigmoidoscopy with mucosal biopsy; Rectal swab culture/Gram stain; Stool Routine & Microscopy
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Massive peranal bleeding; High fever with systemic toxicity; Severe urinary retention; Severe perianal tissue breakdown

Primary_Symptoms: Altered mental status (confusion, disorientation, drowsiness, coma); Flapping tremors (Asterixis); Personality changes
Secondary_Symptoms: Day-night sleep reversal; Slurred speech; Ataxia; Jaundice; Fetor hepaticus
Typical_Duration: Acute emergency overlaying chronic liver disease
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Patient ko uljhan, behoshi ya bhoolne ki bimari achanak hui hai?; 2. Haath me kapaahat (flapping tremor) hai?; 3. Jigar/Liver ki purani bimari hai?
Popular_Indian_Brands: Duphalac Syrup; Rifagut 550; Injection L-Ornithine L-Aspartate (LOLA)
Supportive_Medicines: Lactulose syrup 30-45 mL 2-4 times daily (titrated to 2-3 soft stools/day); Rifaximin 550 mg BD; LOLA IV infusion
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h; NSAIDs and alcohol MUST be strictly avoided; Do NOT give sedatives
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital transfer; Prevent aspiration (turn patient on side if somnolent); Do NOT give oral proteins or solid food during acute stage while reaching hospital
Lab_Investigations: Blood Ammonia levels; Liver Function Test; Serum Electrolytes; Arterial Blood Gas; Brain CT (rule out intracranial bleed)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Unresponsiveness/Coma; Respiratory depression; Seizures; GI bleeding flare

Common_Names_Hindi: Sharab se pet ki sujan; Alcoholic Gastritis
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe burning epigastric pain post alcohol binge; Nausea; Retching
Secondary_Symptoms: Vomiting (sometimes streak of blood); Anorexia; Epigastric tenderness; Bloating
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Zyada sharab peene ke baad pet me tez meetha dard/jalan hui hai?; 2. Ulti aur mithli ho rahi hai?; 3. Khana khane me takleef hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Sucralfate 1g suspension 10 mL QID (before meals); Antacid syrup 10 mL TDS SOS; Thiamine (Vitamin B1) 100 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h in all liver/gastric conditions; NSAIDs and alcohol MUST be strictly avoided
Home_Care_Advice: COMPLETE CESSATION OF ALCOHOL; Sip oral rehydration fluids; Bland soft diet (khichdi, curd-rice); Avoid spicy, acidic, fried food and coffee
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy (if symptoms persist or hematemesis occurs); CBC; LFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Repeated hematemesis (vomiting blood); Melena (black tarry stools); Severe unbearable continuous abdominal pain; Hypotension

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai se pet me acitidy/ulcer; Painkiller Gastritis
Primary_Symptoms: Epigastric pain/burning after taking painkillers (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac, Aspirin); Nausea; Heartburn
Secondary_Symptoms: Dyspepsia; Vomiting; Anorexia; Microscopic or overt GI blood loss
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard ki dawai (painkiller) khane ke baad pet me jalana/dard hua hai?; 2. Ulti ya mithli hoti hai?; 3. Stool ka rang kala to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pantoprazole OR Rabeprazole (plus STOP the offending NSAID)
Supportive_Medicines: Sucralfate 1g suspension 10 mL QID; Rebamipide 100 mg TDS; Switch to Paracetamol for analgesia
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; IMMEDIATELY STOP ALL NSAIDs; Use Paracetamol for pain instead; Long-term PPI needs doctor review
Home_Care_Advice: STRICTLY STOP OFFENDING NSAIDs; Eat bland, soft non-spicy meals; Take all unavoidable drugs with meals/food; Avoid alcohol and coffee
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy; Complete Blood Count (check Hb for anemia); Stool Occult Blood
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hematemesis (vomiting blood or coffee-ground material); Melena (black tarry stools); Sudden severe sharp abdominal pain (perforation)

Primary_Symptoms: Excessive passage of intestinal gas (flatus); Abdominal bloating/distension; Frequent belching
Secondary_Symptoms: Abdominal rumbling (borborygmi); Mild crampy discomfort; Sensation of fullness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bahut zyada gas pass hoti hai ya dakar aati hai?; 2. Khana jaldi-jaldi khane ki aadat hai?; 3. Pet me gas ki wajah se bhari-pan rehta hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Enzyme combination tablets (Diastase + Pepsin); Probiotics
Precautions_Contraindications: Differentiate simple aerophagia/flatulence from organic GI disease; Avoid long-term charcoal without medical advice as it adsorbs other medications
Home_Care_Advice: Eat slowly and chew food thoroughly; Avoid carbonated drinks, chewing gum, and drinking through straws; Limit gas-forming foods (beans, cabbage, onions, radishes)
Lab_Investigations: None routinely required unless red flags present
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe abdominal pain; Unintentional weight loss; Persistent vomiting; Blood in stool; Change in bowel habits in older adults

Primary_Symptoms: Painful bulge in groin/scrotum worsening on standing, coughing, or straining; Heavy groin sensation
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild dragging ache; Bulge reduces when lying flat; Local discomfort
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhatia/Groin me koi ganth/soojan hai jo khade hone ya khansne par badhti hai?; 2. Letne par ganth andar chali jati hai?; 3. Dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol (for symptomatic pain relief prior to elective surgery)
Supportive_Medicines: Truss belt (temporary conservative measure under surgical guidance); Osmotic laxatives (to prevent straining)
Precautions_Contraindications: Medications do NOT cure hernia - Definitive cure is Surgical Hernioplasty; Do NOT forcefully push back painful non-reducible bulge; Avoid NSAIDs if GI risk
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid heavy weight lifting, strenuous exercise, and coughing; Treat chronic cough and constipation to prevent straining; Wear supportive groin truss if advised
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Abdomen & Scrotum (Groin USG); Surgical Consultation
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Emergency surgical referral if hernia becomes irreducible, excruciatingly painful, red, with vomiting and inability to pass gas/stool (Strangulated Hernia)

Common_Names_Hindi: Hiatal Hernia; Pet ka upar khisakna
Primary_Symptoms: Severe persistent heartburn; Regurgitation of food/acid into mouth; Epigastric pain; Dysphagia
Secondary_Symptoms: Early satiety; Postprandial fullness; Belching; Retrosternal burning; Hiccups
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khana khane ke baad gale me sara hua khana/tezaab aata hai?; 2. Letne ya jhukne par chhati me jalana badhti hai?; 3. Upper GI X-ray/Endoscopy hui hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Sodium Alginate syrup 10 mL post meals & bedtime; Magaldrate syrup SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Long-term PPI use needs doctor review; Surgical evaluation (Fundoplication) if severe refractory symptoms
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate head end of bed by 6-8 inches; Eat small frequent meals; Do NOT lie down within 3 hours of eating; Avoid tight clothing around waist; Avoid bending forward post meals
Lab_Investigations: Upper GI Endoscopy; Barium Swallow X-ray; High-Resolution Esophageal Manometry
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) or food impaction; Vomiting blood; Severe chest pain; Unexplained weight loss

Common_Names_Hindi: Bina kisi waja ka pet dard; Functional Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent or continuous abdominal pain without organic cause on testing; Intermittent cramps
Secondary_Symptoms: Associated anxiety/stress; Fatigue; Dyspepsia; Headaches; Sleep disturbance
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet me dard mahino se hai par saari reports normal aayi hain?; 2. Chinta ya stress hone par dard badhta hai?; 3. Latrine hone par bhi dard me farak nahi padta?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Hyoscine butylbromide OR Mebeverine (plus Low-dose Amitriptyline)
Supportive_Medicines: Probiotics; Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Peppermint oil capsules
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 30 mg Hyoscine / 405 mg Mebeverine / 25 mg Amitriptyline
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Reassure patient regarding benign nature after ruling out organic pathology; Caution with TCAs in glaucoma and cardiac conduction defects
Home_Care_Advice: Stress management (meditation, yoga); Regular mild exercise; Balanced regular meals; Avoid unnecessary repetitive invasive diagnostic tests
Lab_Investigations: CBC; ESR/CRP; Stool Routine; USG Abdomen; Celiac serology (All normal in functional pain)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Appearance of new red flag signs (fever, weight loss, nocturnal pain awakening from sleep, GI bleeding, jaundice)

Primary_Symptoms: Inability to pass stool for days; Severe rectal fullness/pressure; Paradoxical overflow diarrhea
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe abdominal distension; Cramping; Nausea; Urinary retention; Confusion in elderly
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kai dinon se latrine nahi hui hai aur anus me bada kada mal atka lagta hai?; 2. Patli watery latrine automatic raste se ris (leak) rahi hai?; 3. Pet fula hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Glycerin Suppository OR Phosphate Enema (plus manual disimpaction by healthcare provider)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Glycerin Suppositories Adult; Practo-Clyss Enema; Enema Express
Supportive_Medicines: Polyethylene Glycol (PEG 3350) 17g BD post clearance; Stool softeners
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use aggressive oral stimulant laxatives BEFORE clearing rectal impaction (can cause stercoral perforation); Caution with phosphate enemas in renal impairment
Home_Care_Advice: Manual digital evacuation under medical supervision if needed; Follow with high fluid and PEG regimen; High fiber diet post-clearance
Lab_Investigations: Abdominal Plain X-ray (KUB showing mass fecal load in rectum/colon); Digital Rectal Examination (DRE)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Stercoral perforation signs (sudden severe abdominal pain, board-like rigidity, shock); High fever; Massive rectal bleeding

Primary_Symptoms: Asymptomatic or mild fluctuating jaundice (scleral icterus) during stress, fasting, or illness
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild fatigue; Mild abdominal discomfort; Normal physical examination; No liver disease
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peeli aankhein fasting, bukhar ya stress ke waqt achanak dikhti hain?; 2. Baaki liver report bilkul normal hai?; 3. Baraf ya bukhar ke baad peela-pan badhta hai?
Supportive_Medicines: B-complex vitamins for reassurance
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h; Absolute reassurance that condition is completely benign and non-progressive; Avoid prolonged fasting or extreme exertion
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain regular balanced diet; Avoid prolonged fasting or strict low-calorie crash diets; Hydrate well; Avoid excessive physical/emotional stress
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test (Unconjugated/Indirect Hyperbilirubinemia strictly <3-4 mg/dL with normal ALT, AST, Alkaline Phosphatase, and Albumin); Normal CBC
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Direct/Conjugated Bilirubin elevation; High AST/ALT; Fever with dark urine and pale stools (indicates true liver pathology, not Gilbert's)

Primary_Symptoms: Acute jaundice; Nausea; Vomiting; Anorexia; Epigastric/RUQ abdominal discomfort
Secondary_Symptoms: Malaise; Dark urine; Pale stools; Pruritus; Rash; Fever
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koi nayi dawai (Paracetamol overdose, TB meds, Herbal/Ayurvedic) li thi?; 2. Aankhein peeli hui hain?; 3. Ulti aur bhookh kam lagna shuru hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC - specifically for Paracetamol) OR Ursodeoxycholic Acid + STOP SUSPECTED DRUG
Supportive_Medicines: L-Ornithine L-Aspartate (LOLA); B-complex vitamins; Antiemetics (Ondansetron 4 mg)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; IMMEDIATELY DISCONTINUE SUSPECTED HEPATOTOXIC DRUG; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h; NSAIDs and alcohol MUST be strictly avoided
Home_Care_Advice: STRICTLY STOP OFFENDING DRUG/HERBAL SUPPLEMENT; Complete rest; High carbohydrate low-fat diet; Total abstinence from alcohol
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test (marked AST/ALT/Bilirubin elevation); INR/Prothrombin Time; Viral Hepatitis Serologies (to rule out viral cause); USG Abdomen
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rapidly deepening jaundice with encephalopathy (confusion, drowsiness); Coagulopathy (bleeding/bruising); Severe intractable vomiting

Common_Names_Hindi: Hepatitis B; Kalimati; Jigar ka infection
Primary_Symptoms: Often asymptomatic; Chronic fatigue; Anorexia; Mild RUQ discomfort; Jaundice (in flares)
Secondary_Symptoms: Hepatomegaly; Splenomegaly; Palmar erythema; Spider nevi; Dark urine
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) positive aaya hai?; 2. Purani thakan ya peela-pan rehta hai?; 3. Parivaar me kisi ko Hepatitis B hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Ursodeoxycholic Acid 300 mg BD; B-complex; Hepatoprotectants
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Do not abruptly stop antiviral therapy (causes severe acute hepatitis flare); Renal function and bone density monitoring with Tenofovir; Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Complete lifelong adherence to antivirals; Zero alcohol intake; Vaccinate family members/close contacts against Hepatitis B; Do not share razors/needles
Lab_Investigations: HBsAg; HBeAg; HBV DNA Quantitative Real-Time PCR; Liver Function Test; USG Abdomen; FibroScan; Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Decompensation signs (ascites, jaundice, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy); Acute flare up with severe jaundice and vomiting

Common_Names_Hindi: Hepatitis C; Hepatitis C ka infection
Primary_Symptoms: Often asymptomatic for decades; Chronic fatigue; Myalgia; Arthralgia; Mild RUQ pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Jaundice (late stage); Anorexia; Weight loss; Cirrhosis complications
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Anti-HCV blood test positive aaya hai?; 2. Kabhi blood transfusion ya surgery hui hai?; 3. Thakan rehti hai?
Supportive_Medicines: Ursodeoxycholic Acid 300 mg BD; Multivitamins
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Direct-Acting Antivirals cure >95% of cases; Test for HBV co-infection before starting (risk of HBV reactivation); Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Strict daily adherence to 12-week course without missing doses; Total alcohol abstinence; Avoid sharing personal care items (razors, toothbrushes)
Lab_Investigations: Anti-HCV Antibody; HCV RNA Quantitative PCR; HCV Genotype; Liver Function Test; USG Abdomen; FibroScan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Signs of liver decompensation (ascites, jaundice, bleeding, encephalopathy); Suspected hepatocellular carcinoma

Primary_Symptoms: Acute jaundice (scleral icterus & dark urine); Severe anorexia; Nausea; Vomiting; RUQ pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Fever; Malaise; Pruritus; Clay-colored stools; Hepatomegaly
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peeli aankhein aur kaala/peela peshab hai?; 2. Khana dekhkar ulti aati hai?; 3. Dushit paani ya bahar ka food khaya tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Symptomatic supportive treatment - NO SPECIFIC ANTIVIRAL NEEDED
Supportive_Medicines: Ondansetron 4 mg SOS; B-complex vitamins; Hydration (ORS)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; HIGH MORTALITY IN PREGNANT WOMEN (up to 20-25% risk of fulminant hepatic failure in 3rd trimester); Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Complete physical bed rest; High carbohydrate, low-fat diet; Drink boiled water; Absolute avoidance of alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs
Lab_Investigations: IgM Anti-HEV Antibody; Liver Function Test (SGOT/SGPT often >1000 U/L, High Bilirubin); PT/INR; USG Abdomen
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Any pregnant woman with Hepatitis E (Urgent admission); Drowsiness/confusion (encephalopathy); Bleeding manifestations; Persistent severe vomiting

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai se dast; Antibiotic Diarrhea / C. difficile
Primary_Symptoms: Watery loose stools developing during or after antibiotic course; Abdominal cramps
Secondary_Symptoms: Low fever; Nausea; Bloating; Leukocytosis; Mucus in stool
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koi antibiotic (Cefixime, Augmentin, Clindamycin) chal rahi hai?; 2. Din me kitni baar loose motion ho raha hai?; 3. Pet me marod hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Saccharomyces boulardii OR Oral Vancomycin / Metronidazole (if C. difficile severe)
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS); Zinc 20 mg OD; Discontinue offending antibiotic if possible
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; STOP offending broad-spectrum antibiotic if clinically safe; Do NOT give anti-motility agents (Loperamide) in C. difficile colitis (risk of toxic megacolon)
